listing.name: Monster Hunter Portable 3rd HD Ver. Yakumo
listing.summary: Play your Monster Hunter Portable 3rd HD disc image with Yakumo. Use Yakumo to prepare the game and keep its saves.

steps.title: Complete the exact owned-input preparation upstream
steps.instruction: Use the PSP UMD image from your own Monster Hunter Portable 3rd HD Ver. PS3 release (NPJB-40001). Choose the uncompressed ISO in Yakumo and let it prepare the game. The ordinary PSP edition, a whole PS3 disc image and compressed CSO files are different inputs.

steps.title: Add a prepared Windows installation to Portcove
steps.instruction: Select Yakumo.exe in its complete creating Windows folder, keeping its matching overlay libraries, FFmpeg DLLs, fonts and resources. Use that folder as working directory and no extra arguments for a normal already-prepared copy. Retain supported literal --data-dir or existing game-directory arguments only if that working copy already uses them; do not silently change the creating data or save roots. Review the program, start folder and launch options, then add the game and choose Play.

steps.title: Set up Yakumo on Linux or Steam Deck
steps.instruction: Open the x64 Flatpak through your desktop or Steam. It uses the Freedesktop Platform 25.08 runtime. If you unpack the x64 tarball, start it with ./yakumo from the unpacked folder so the launcher sets the stack size. The tarball needs glibc 2.29 or later, a Vulkan driver and the Vulkan loader. Use Yakumo for setup and play.

steps.title: Set up Yakumo on an Apple Silicon Mac
steps.instruction: Open the ARM64 disk image on macOS 13 or later and copy Yakumo.app to Applications. Keep the whole app. Open it directly and select your disc image in Yakumo. The publisher uses ad hoc signing. Follow its macOS guide for the first-open prompt.

steps.title: Set up Yakumo on Android
steps.instruction: Install the ARM64 APK on Android 10 or later with Vulkan 1.1. Open Yakumo and choose your ISO in the Android file picker. The app copies it into its own storage, so allow about 1.3 GB for the image in addition to the app. Use Yakumo to back up your saves before replacing or removing the app.

warnings: MIT covers the project’s own original code; third-party IP remains independently owned. Preserve the applicable packaged FFmpeg LGPL and font/dependency notices; this is not a whole-game rights certificate.

Upstream documents untranslated/blank save-dialog screens, curved-surface issues and unsupported code mods; reported rendering, multiplayer, controller and save compatibility are publisher claims, not Portcove observations. No game, original, helper, installer or native session was run.

The Windows installed profile normally uses %APPDATA%/Yakumo/MHP3rd. The portable package uses data/ beside the executable. Existing portable.txt, a data/ folder, --portable, --data-dir and MHP3RD_DATA_DIR/MHP3RD_PORTABLE choices affect selection; retain the actual established mode and do not add/remove markers or trigger profile-copy prompts as registration work. A non-writable portable directory fails instead of silently falling back.

Upstream Set Up Game Data Again and Restart Now after save import can end it and start a successor. Perform those actions outside the attached session; Core does not automatically adopt the successor or offer upstream save import/export, texture installation, backup or network configuration. Retain the old working runtime and all data before replacement.

references.title: Preserve the actual portable or installed profile
references.instruction: The Windows installed profile normally uses %APPDATA%/Yakumo/MHP3rd. The portable package uses data/ beside the executable. Existing portable.txt, a data/ folder, --portable, --data-dir and MHP3RD_DATA_DIR/MHP3RD_PORTABLE choices affect selection; retain the actual established mode and do not add/remove markers or trigger profile-copy prompts as registration work. A non-writable portable directory fails instead of silently falling back. Keep settings.ini, prepared EBOOT.ELF, copied disc.iso or its external in-place original, ms0/PSP/SAVEDATA (including ULJM05800, ULJM05800QST and ULJM05800DAT), mods, texture packs, pipeline caches/keys, logs, controller mappings, translations/fonts, save-backups, temporary files and all custom roots. A source-build game directory may retain its own ms0 and older saves; do not migrate it automatically.

references.title: Check the original-file identity
references.instruction: Yakumo checks NPJB-40001 and encrypted EBOOT.BIN SHA-256 79e25f3512d56e0f7bf5c48351d7d0d255269675ffc8811ac5599322bb66945e, then verifies prepared EBOOT.ELF SHA-256 55c0598436c0753b04331f8e95d406f832d9217806e3a896fed0e88b33637d8c. The check covers those files and the disc ID.

references.title: Find and back up the data you actually use
references.instruction: The Flatpak keeps data in ~/.var/app/io.github.teamgdb.Yakumo/data/Yakumo/MHP3rd and can export saves to Downloads. The Linux tarball uses $XDG_DATA_HOME/Yakumo/MHP3rd or ~/.local/share/Yakumo/MHP3rd by default. The Mac app uses ~/Library/Application Support/Yakumo/MHP3rd. Keep your actual profile and any ISO used in place before replacing the app.
